scenario: An independent recruiter returns between conversations, identifies the one relationship dependency that deserves attention, reviews exact evidence, optionally revises only the proposed interpretation, and separately stages one recruiter-owned draft question without sending or scheduling anything.

review_plan.reason: The surface must reduce reconstruction work and support a bounded recruiter-owned next step.
The core interaction separates source evidence, proposed state, review, and action authority.
The route preserves an existing mobile concept and adds a modal evidence workflow with keyboard and responsive obligations.
Quiet, delay, identity ambiguity, and follow-up language can affect candidate trust even when actions remain recruiter owned.
The artifact does not assess, compare, rank, score, or recommend candidates.
A synthetic search context is present, but the evaluated decision is recruiter workflow and not an account consensus claim.

findings.observation: The executable public concept makes one current dependency, exact evidence, an editable proposed state, and one owned draft action recoverable in a single workspace, but the scenario uses synthetic fixtures and has not been compared with a working recruiter's current fallback.
findings.evidence: Browser run at /relationships; final Today, evidence, revision, Searches, and mobile captures; the tested revision changed only the proposed interpretation and left the source quote unchanged.
findings.user_impact: The workflow is operationally coherent, but claims that it saves time or prevents a missed candidate window remain unproven in real search work.
findings.recommendation: Run a five-minute pre-call recovery comparison with independent recruiters using their normal chat, notes, calendar, and ATS fallback.
findings.verification: In at least five consented cases, measure time to identify the current dependency, seeded-error correction, unnecessary follow-up avoided, and whether the proposed action changes the recruiter's next real step.

findings.observation: Navigation, evidence decisions, revised wording, and staged actions remain coherent while the concept is open, but a page reload intentionally returns to the default synthetic state.
findings.evidence: Browser execution covered Today to evidence review to revision to action staging and cross-surface navigation; reload reset local fixture state as designed for the public walkthrough.
findings.user_impact: A visitor loses demo progress after refresh; the same behavior would be unacceptable in the authenticated recruiter workspace.
findings.recommendation: Keep the public walkthrough ephemeral and require versioned server persistence plus a visible resume receipt before reusing it for live recruiter work.
findings.verification: In an authenticated implementation, revise or dismiss one proposal, reload, return after a day, and confirm that the exact version, action boundary, and current external state are restored without duplication.

strengths: Today limits attention to one dominant dependency and two secondary relationships instead of presenting a broad CRM dashboard.
People and Searches preserve the same synthetic relationship state while changing the organizing context.
Exact evidence, before and proposed values, revision, dismissal, and keep decisions stay in one focused review sheet.
The next move remains disabled until the evidence proposal is kept or revised, and staging never claims that anything was sent or scheduled.
Quiet and unresolved-identity states remove the action instead of manufacturing urgency.
missing_evidence: Working-recruiter comparison against the current manual fallback.
Authenticated persistence and day-later interruption recovery.
Measured action completion and avoided-follow-up outcomes.
open_questions: Which three dependency types most often deserve a place on Today for an independent recruiter?
Should the authenticated product remember a staged question as a private draft or only after an explicit save decision?

reviews.lens: evidence integrity, privacy, and safe action

findings.observation: The review sheet keeps the exact synthetic quote, source type, timestamp, review status, before value, and proposed value together, and a wording revision changes only the proposed interpretation. It does not expose a source asset identifier, captured span coordinates, model or policy version, or append-only edit history because this is a non-persisting public concept.
findings.evidence: The implemented component and revision screenshot show the source quote remaining fixed while only revised wording is editable.
findings.user_impact: The public walkthrough teaches the correct boundary, but the same treatment would be insufficient proof for a real candidate fact without deeper provenance and supersession history.
findings.recommendation: When connecting the surface to live data, add stable source and assertion identifiers, derivation version, confirmer, edit event, and superseding event without crowding the primary decision.
findings.verification: Replay one imported source through extraction, recruiter revision, dismissal, and supersession; every displayed state must resolve to the exact versioned source and append-only decision event.

findings.observation: The page explicitly states that the walkthrough is synthetic and stores no candidate data, and capture and voice controls return no-op permission receipts. Storage, retention, export, and deletion are intentionally absent rather than proven.
findings.evidence: Visible synthetic-data notice, no-op capture receipt, and absence of connector or persistence calls in the component.
findings.user_impact: There is no private-data lifecycle risk in this concept, but the screen cannot prove that a future production implementation deletes raw and derived data correctly.
findings.recommendation: Keep lifecycle claims out of this public artifact and bind any authenticated implementation to the repository's authorization, retention, export, and deletion contracts.
findings.verification: Import and delete a consented test source in the authenticated product; raw asset, derived assertion, cache, index, and audit handling must match the disclosed policy and purpose.

strengths: An unresolved mixed-script identity removes every dependent action and asks for identity resolution before attachment.
Observed evidence, proposed interpretation, user revision, and draft action are visually and behaviorally distinct.
Keeping or revising a proposal does not approve the next action; dismissing it retracts the dependent draft.
Action state resets when the selected person or search changes, preventing cross-object authorization leakage.
Capture, voice, command, and staging controls explicitly deny external write authority and never claim an unverified result.
No candidate quality, fit, personality, protected trait, engagement, or acceptance score appears anywhere in the surface.
missing_evidence: Production asset, assertion, derivation, edit, and supersession identifiers.
Retention, export, deletion, backup, and vendor lifecycle evidence.
External-write idempotency, reconciliation, and reversal evidence, which remain out of scope for this draft-only concept.
open_questions: Which provenance fields should remain one click away versus visible in the first review viewport?
How should a recruiter compare a revised interpretation with a later contradictory source without flattening either event?

reviews.lens: mobile task completion, visual hierarchy, accessibility, and recovery

findings.observation: The responsive route exposes labeled controls, a modal dialog with focus trapping and focus return, reduced-motion behavior, dark mode, text alternatives, and no horizontal overflow at 375, 390, 844-landscape, 1024, and 1440 pixels. A real screen-reader session and browser zoom matrix beyond simulated 200 percent root text were not available.
findings.evidence: Browser runs, responsive captures, reduced-motion inspection, Lighthouse accessibility 100, and ten visible mobile controls measuring at least 44 by 44 pixels.
findings.user_impact: The critical path is structurally accessible, but a screen-reader or switch user could still encounter an ordering or announcement problem that automated inspection cannot prove absent.
findings.recommendation: Run VoiceOver or an equivalent screen reader through Today, evidence review, revision, dismissal, People, and Searches before treating this as release-level accessibility proof.
findings.verification: Complete the critical path using only screen reader and keyboard input; identity, source, proposed state, consequence, and every decision must be announced once in visual order, and focus must return to the invoking control.

findings.observation: The final production Lighthouse run scored 97 performance on desktop and 92 on mobile; mobile LCP was 3.0 seconds while CLS remained zero.
findings.evidence: Final desktop and mobile Lighthouse JSON generated against a clean production Next.js server.
findings.user_impact: The product concept remains responsive after load, but slower mobile connections may delay the first meaningful marketing heading enough to weaken perceived quality.
findings.recommendation: Profile route-level global CSS and shared client JavaScript, then defer below-fold relationship concept code where it does not compromise server-rendered meaning.
findings.verification: Repeat mobile Lighthouse and a throttled browser trace three times; median LCP must be at most 2.5 seconds, CLS remain zero, and no product interaction may be delayed or removed.

strengths: The evidence sheet uses the Shadcn-compatible Radix dialog primitive for semantic naming, inert background, focus trapping, Escape dismissal, and exact focus return.
The route switches cleanly to the existing phone concept below 900 pixels and shows no horizontal overflow at 375, 390, or 844-landscape viewports.
A simulated 200 percent root text size preserved the mobile product without horizontal overflow; a discovered footer overflow was corrected and retested.
All ten visible mobile product buttons measured at least 44 by 44 pixels in the 200 percent text scenario.
Light, dark, reduced-motion, long mixed-script identity, missing avatar, empty search, no-action, and unresolved-identity states were inspected.
Final Lighthouse scored accessibility, best practices, and SEO at 100 on desktop and mobile.
missing_evidence: Repeated mobile performance traces after route-level CSS and JavaScript profiling.
Real-device browser safe-area, virtual-keyboard, and touch ergonomics.
Simplified Chinese localization expansion and RTL behavior.
open_questions: Should the public route load only the currently applicable desktop or mobile product implementation to reduce below-fold code on slower devices?
Which mobile state should remain visible when a recruiter returns after an interruption in the authenticated product?

reviews.lens: human connection, trust, agency, communication, collaboration

findings.observation: The interface protects candidate time through specific ownership, quiet and no-action outcomes, exact unresolved dependencies, and candidate-specific commitments, but these behaviors have only been exercised with synthetic people and have not been reviewed by candidates or working recruiters.
findings.evidence: Executable scenarios for Leila, Nia, Maya, Amir, and an unresolved mixed-script identity; Amir shows no reminder due and protection from premature follow-up with no action control.
findings.user_impact: The design avoids obvious pressure and ghosting patterns, but its language and timing cannot yet be claimed to feel considerate in a real consequential search.
findings.recommendation: Test the dependency, quiet, contradiction, and identity language with recruiters and candidate advisors using consented or synthetic scenarios before carrying the copy into candidate-facing operations.
findings.verification: Participants must correctly identify who owns the delay, what remains unknown, whether a candidate will be contacted, and how to stop or correct the action without interpreting silence as rejection.

findings.observation: The current smallest step is a recruiter-owned question to the client and remains a private draft; no candidate-facing message, channel, time, or recipient is previewed because candidate communication is outside this concept's boundary.
findings.evidence: Right-rail copy states that nothing is sent or scheduled; the enabled control stages an exact question and the status keeps a separate human decision explicit.
findings.user_impact: No candidate is affected by the concept, but a future message action could erode trust if it reused the same button without an exact recipient and message preview.
findings.recommendation: Require a separate candidate-facing preview with recipient, channel, timing, editable wording, cancel, and verified result before any communication capability is added.
findings.verification: Attempt a candidate message from every current state; the system must stop at a complete editable preview, never use silence as a negative signal, and never send after permission or context changes.

strengths: Quiet is a deliberate successful outcome, not an engagement failure or invitation to nudge again.
The interface assigns the unresolved dependency to the recruiter, client, founder, or board instead of making the candidate carry internal delay.
Each person and search carries its own commitment, due state, protected human outcome, and waiting reason, preventing pressure from leaking between relationships.
Uncertain identity is left unresolved and cannot acquire a relationship action.
No response-speed, engagement, fit, quality, culture, personality, or acceptance inference is present.
Automation removes reconstruction work while every consequential relationship decision remains human-owned.
missing_evidence: Candidate or candidate-advisor comprehension of the language and timing.
Working-recruiter evidence that quiet states prevent unnecessary outreach.
Candidate-facing preview, delivery, failure, correction, and closure behavior, which remain out of scope.
open_questions: When should a quiet state remind the recruiter to update the candidate even if no new decision evidence exists?
Which internal owner should be visible when a client or hiring-manager delay risks becoming candidate silence?

top_findings.reason: Synthetic task completion proves coherence but not reduced recruiter reconstruction time or better real next decisions.
top_findings.next_step: Run a five-minute comparison against each recruiter's current fallback in at least five consented cases.
top_findings.verification: Measure recovery time, correction of seeded errors, unnecessary follow-up avoided, and whether the proposed action changes the next real step.

top_findings.reason: Automated accessibility and keyboard evidence cannot prove announcement order or switch-control completion.
top_findings.next_step: Complete the evidence review and recovery path with VoiceOver or equivalent assistive technology.
top_findings.verification: Identity, exact source, proposed state, consequence, and decisions are announced once in visual order and focus returns correctly.

top_findings.reason: Final mobile Lighthouse performance is 92 with 3.0 second LCP, below the requested 95-plus objective even though accessibility, best practices, and SEO are 100.
top_findings.next_step: Profile route-level CSS and shared client JavaScript, then repeat three mobile production traces.
top_findings.verification: Median mobile LCP is at most 2.5 seconds, CLS remains zero, and the relationship interaction keeps full meaning and behavior.

agreements: Exact evidence, proposed interpretation, human review, and action staging remain distinct in both copy and behavior.
No public control sends, schedules, persists, or silently approves a consequential action.
Quiet and unresolved identity are safe first-class outcomes without manufactured urgency.
The surface ranks work attention and never scores, ranks, or predicts a person's worth, fit, personality, or acceptance.
The local visual and interaction slice is complete enough to test with users, but not to support production or commercial outcome claims.
adjudication.rationale: All four applicable reviewers score the bounded local artifact 3 of 4 with no vetoes. Browser, build, test, responsive, keyboard, and Lighthouse evidence support a coherent high-quality public concept. The release gate remains needs_evidence because real recruiter value, candidate comprehension, authenticated provenance, assistive-technology completion, and mobile performance at the requested threshold are not yet proven.

next_tests.test: Five-minute pre-call reconstruction comparison with at least five independent recruiters.
next_tests.evidence_required: Consented task recordings, current-fallback baseline, seeded-error results, and observed next-step changes.
next_tests.pass_condition: The desk reduces median recovery time or prevents a material evidence/action error without increasing unnecessary outreach.

next_tests.test: VoiceOver and keyboard completion of evidence keep, revision, dismissal, action staging, quiet, and unresolved-identity paths.
next_tests.evidence_required: Screen-reader transcript or recording, focus order, announcements, and interruption recovery on a supported real device or simulator.
next_tests.pass_condition: Every critical state is announced once in visual order, every decision is operable, no focus is lost, and no hidden action becomes available.

next_tests.test: Three throttled production mobile traces after profiling shared CSS and client JavaScript.
next_tests.evidence_required: Lighthouse JSON and performance trace for each run with the LCP element and route payload identified.
next_tests.pass_condition: Median performance is at least 95, median LCP is at most 2.5 seconds, CLS is zero, and functional parity is preserved.
